pageCache.pageTitle: St Michael's C.E. Primary School  - Collective Worship
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
At St Michael's, we gather every day for a special time of worship. It's a time when all of us, both students and teachers, come together to learn and reflect. Although our collective worship is distinctly Christian in nature; there is freedom within both prayer and reflection times to worship in other ways. Our nurturing ethos rooted in God’s value enables all members of our school community to thrive and flourish, becoming compassionate and responsible members of society.
Our pattern of weekly worship is as follows:
‘Big’ Assembly with Infants, Juniors and Reception with Praise assembly focusing on key themes linked to the liturgical calendar
Whole School Music Collective Worship
St Paul's Cathedral Music Teacher
Lower School CW based on values theme
Upper School CW based on values theme
Teachers according to rota
Pupil-Led Collective Worship in class
Big’ Assembly with Infants and Juniors using Picture News incorporating current issues in the World with values/Bible verse
Our Worship Policy follows the guidelines of the Education Acts of 1944 and 1988, and it aligns with the tenets of the Church of England as stated in our trust deed. It is available to read below together with our Spirituality Policy.

About Us
It is an honour to be the Headteacher of such a fantastic school community and on behalf of the staff, governors and children, I’d like to welcome you to our website, to give you an insight into life here at St Michael’s.
At St Michael’s we have tasked ourselves with the responsibility of enabling children to be a 'force for positive change'. We believe that our curriculum encompasses all that the children need to become happy, confident outstanding pillars of the community. As adults, we lead by example and demonstrate a working environment where the children see positive working relationships, collaboration between staff and shared vision.
Our curriculum is relevant and purposeful; whilst focusing on all aspects of the national curriculum, we strive to ensure that children feel valued and celebrated by what they are taught. Our Christian ethos runs through our curriculum with teachings from the church underpinning all aspects and explorations of different beliefs and religions. Our motto ‘Seek Joy in Service’ lends itself to teaching our children the importance of contributing to the wider community. St Michael’s Church and Father Stephen are very much part of our extended family and all who join us are welcome there regardless of faith, religion or background.
As a school we offer a wonderfully green site in Enfield, which provides a great setting for your children to have excellent indoor and outdoor experiences. The local amenities also allow us to take advantage of further outdoor learning opportunities.
We give children the space to feel safe and confident and pride ourselves on exploring the wider curriculum with residentials, performances and experiences that focus on ‘the whole child.’
We believe this is a wonderful school and are proud of all we do for the children here. We very much welcome visits to the school, so if you would like to find out more, please contact us to make an appointment and we would love to show you around.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Michael's C.E. Primary School  - Club St Michael's
pageCache.text:
Club St Michael's
Our After School Club and an additional Breakfast Club are run by J&L Out of School Ltd.
Here they try to answer some of the questions you might have:
Who are J&L Out of School Ltd?
J&L Out of School Ltd are a local privately owned company providing quality After School Clubs, Breakfast Clubs and (where there is demand) Holiday Clubs. We have been operating at St. Michael’s for 10 years and are proud to say that we have become a very close part of St. Michael’s community.
Our aim is to create and deliver thoughtful and engaging programmes for children at the school, providing them with an opportunity for informal learning, as well as to relax and have fun.
We share the same ethos and values as St. Michael’s and that is why our club is called simply Club St. Michael’s – although it should be stressed that we are a separate entity from the school.
Where does Club St. Michael’s take place?
Our breakfast club is run from the St. Michael’s and All Angels Church Hall at the bottom of Gordon Hill. The after school club is run from the school dining room.
What happens at Club St. Michael’s?
We offer children an opportunity to participate in a wide variety of activities in a fun, safe and engaging way. At a session, children are given the opportunity to relax and select what they would like to do from a wide selection of toys and games plus they are invited to participate in organised activities based upon topical themes.
From 7.45am each morning you will be able to drop your children at Breakfast Club (at the St. Michael’s Church Hall) where they will enjoy a breakfast comprising a choice of cereals with toast plus juice, milk or water to drink. We then walk the children, in a group, up to school in time for registration. Both the Breakfast Club and After School Club are solely for St Michael’s children.
At After School Club, as well as free play, children can complete homework or so some quiet reading and we always include the opportunity for them to play physical games either indoors or out. Food has an important role to play and at every session we provide healthy options for tea-time snack and rigidly follow school’s dietary policy.
What are the opening hours and charges?
Regular bookings: 7.45am-8.50am – £5.50. Ad’hoc booking: 7.45am-8.50am – £6.50.
Early session 3.20pm until 5.00pm: £10.00 (regular bookings); £11.00 (ad’hoc bookings). Late session 4.30pm until 6.00pm: £10.00 (regular bookings); £11.00 (ad’hoc bookings). Full session 3.20pm until 6.00pm: £13.00 (regular bookings); £14.00 (ad’hoc bookings).
We offer a 10% discount for siblings who make a Permanent Booking.
Childcare vouchers are accepted and you can make payments using the Tax Free Childcare scheme.
Is Club St Michael’s Ofsted registered?
Yes, we are Ofsted registered and comply with government regulations on how to care for groups of children aged 4-11 years. Our last Ofsted inspection at St. Michael’s can be read here. Club St Michael's - Open - Find an Inspection Report - Ofsted .
The Ofsted registration number for Club St. Michael’s is: 2604801.
Are the staff qualified?
All our staff meet the qualification and experience requirements laid down by Ofsted. Furthermore, our staff undergo a hand selected recruitment and training process that involves the following:
Our training includes: Behaviour Management, Food Safety, Safeguarding and more.
What is the staff to child ratio?
Ofsted allow a staff ratio of 1:30 for out of school hours’ childcare. Club St. Michael’s will always have a higher staff ratio than that. Our minimum is around 1:15 but we are flexible with this to ensure the safety of the children and quality of service.
Who is eligible to enrol at Club St Michael’s?
Any child attending Reception Year or above at the school is eligible to enrol. We strongly recommend that an enrolment form is filled out for every pupil in the school whether you intend to use the service or not. This proves to be helpful in some unforeseen circumstances where a parent may require our services at short notice. No child may attend unless we have a completed enrolment form for them. All details will be uploaded onto our secure software and paper copies are stored in a locked cabinet and only used in accordance with our confidentiality policy and GDPR.
Parents of children in Reception please note that your children are not permitted to attend breakfast and after school club until they are attending classes for the full school day. This is to give them the chance to become acclimatised to the school before they are exposed to an extended school day.
How do I enrol my child and is there a waiting list?
Just complete and return our enrolment form. You can download it here. Alternatively, hard copies of the forms are available from the school office, or you can request one by email from office@jandloutofschool.onmicrosoft.com
A parent handbook will be sent to you by email.
The clubs are very popular and waiting lists operate on certain days where demand exceeds the number of spaces available. Our best advice is to complete an enrolment form and get your name down as early as possible.
What if I’ve got further questions?
For more information please contact John Geers at john@jandloutofschool.onmicrosoft.com or call 07803 887610.

Curriculum
St Michael’s Curriculum Design
At St Michael’s, our curriculum adheres to the National Curriculum and is shaped by our vision and values. Our school’s vision — “We are forces for positive change; we act justly, show merciful love, and walk humbly with our God” — along with our core values of Love, Respect, and Integrity, form the foundation of our curriculum design. These principles guide not only what we teach, but also how we approach learning, character development, and community engagement.
Being Forces for Positive Change
We are committed to preparing students to be active, responsible citizens who engage thoughtfully with the world. Our Open Worlds Humanities, HEP Science and Jigsaw programmes play a key role in this:
Justice is embedded in how and what we teach:
Showing Merciful Love
Compassion and empathy underpin our learning culture:
Walking Humbly with God
Spiritual development is interwoven into school life:
Living the Values of Love, Respect, and Integrity
Our values are lived out through both the content and culture of our curriculum:
By anchoring our curriculum in our vision and values — and enhancing it through rich, contextual programmes like Jigsaw and Open Worlds — we help pupils become thoughtful, compassionate, and courageous learners, ready to contribute meaningfully to the world around them.
'Education is our passport to the future. For tomorrow belongs only to the people who prepare for it today.' Malcolm X

SEND
At St Michael’s Primary School, we strive to meet the needs of all pupils within our school. All staff are aware of SEND within the school and receive high quality information and training.
We aim to quickly identify pupils who are making limited progress and provide targeted interventions and support to meet their needs.
We ensure that parents are fully aware of the SEND process and informed of their child’s learning regularly throughout the year.
We are a fully inclusive school and have strong links with the Local Authority, Health Professionals and organisations within our community. Our environment at St Michael’s Primary School, is developing regularly and consciously to meet the needs of our pupils. We aim to continue to learn, develop and grow our understanding of SEND across the school to meet the needs of all pupils within our care.
